message.content:
Search this repository for a Markdown processing interface/abstraction. I need to find:
1. An interface or trait or abstract class related to markdown processing/rendering/parsing
2. Concrete implementations of that interface
3. Who constructs/instantiates those implementations
4. Which components hold references to the interface

Search broadly - look for things like "MarkdownProcessor", "MarkdownRenderer", "MarkdownParser", "Markdown" combined with interface/trait/abstract/impl patterns. Check in all languages (Rust, TypeScript, etc.). Search breadth: very thorough.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	package renderer
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	
8		gast "github.com/yuin/goldmark/ast"
9		east "github.com/yuin/goldmark/extension/ast"
10	
11		mast "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown/ast"
12	)
13	
14	// MarkdownRenderer renders goldmark AST back to markdown text.
15	type MarkdownRenderer struct {
16		buf *bytes.Buffer
17	}
18	
19	// NewMarkdownRenderer creates a new markdown renderer.
20	func NewMarkdownRenderer() *MarkdownRenderer {
21		return &MarkdownRenderer{
22			buf: &bytes.Buffer{},
23		}
24	}
25	
26	// Render renders the AST node to markdown and returns the result.
27	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) Render(node gast.Node, source []byte) string {
28		r.buf.Reset()
29		r.renderNode(node, source, 0)
30		return r.buf.String()
31	}
32	
33	// renderNode renders a single node and its children.
34	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderNode(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
35		switch n := node.(type) {
36		case *gast.Document:
37			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
38	
39		case *gast.Paragraph:
40			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
41			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
42				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
43			}
44	
45		case *gast.Text:
46			// Text nodes store their content as segments in the source
47			segment := n.Segment
48			r.buf.Write(segment.Value(source))
49			if n.SoftLineBreak() {
50				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
51			} else if n.HardLineBreak() {
52				r.buf.WriteString("  \n")
53			}
54	
55		case *gast.CodeSpan:
56			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
57			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
58			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
59	
60		case *gast.Emphasis:
61			symbol := "*"
62			if n.Level == 2 {
63				symbol = "**"
64			}
65			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
66			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
67			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
68	
69		case *gast.Link:
70			r.buf.WriteString("[")
71			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
72			r.buf.WriteString("](")
73			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
74			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
75				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
76				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
77				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
78			}
79			r.buf.WriteString(")")
80	
81		case *gast.AutoLink:
82			url := n.URL(source)
83			if n.AutoLinkType == gast.AutoLinkEmail {
84				r.buf.WriteString("<")
85				r.buf.Write(url)
86				r.buf.WriteString(">")
87			} else {
88				r.buf.Write(url)
89			}
90	
91		case *gast.Image:
92			r.buf.WriteString("![")
93			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
94			r.buf.WriteString("](")
95			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
96			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
97				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
98				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
99				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
100			}
101			r.buf.WriteString(")")
102	
103		case *gast.Heading:
104			r.buf.WriteString(strings.Repeat("#", n.Level))
105			r.buf.WriteByte(' ')
106			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
107			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
108				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
109			}
110	
111		case *gast.CodeBlock, *gast.FencedCodeBlock:
112			r.renderCodeBlock(n, source)
113	
114		case *gast.Blockquote:
115			// Render each child line with "> " prefix
116			r.renderBlockquote(n, source, depth)
117			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
118				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
119			}
120	
121		case *gast.List:
122			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
123			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
124				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
125			}
126	
127		case *gast.ListItem:
128			r.renderListItem(n, source, depth)
129	
130		case *gast.ThematicBreak:
131			r.buf.WriteString("---")
132			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
133				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
134			}
135	
136		case *east.Strikethrough:
137			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
138			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
139			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
140	
141		case *east.TaskCheckBox:
142			if n.IsChecked {
143				r.buf.WriteString("[x] ")
144			} else {
145				r.buf.WriteString("[ ] ")
146			}
147	
148		case *east.Table:
149			r.renderTable(n, source)
150			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
151				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
152			}
153	
154		// Custom Memos nodes
155		case *mast.TagNode:
156			r.buf.WriteByte('#')
157			r.buf.Write(n.Tag)
158	
159		case *mast.MentionNode:
160			r.buf.WriteByte('@')
161			r.buf.Write(n.Username)
162	
163		default:
164			// For unknown nodes, try to render children
165			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
166		}
167	}
168	
169	// renderChildren renders all children of a node.
170	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderChildren(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
171		child := node.FirstChild()
172		for child != nil {
173			r.renderNode(child, source, depth+1)
174			child = child.NextSibling()
175		}
176	}
177	
178	// renderCodeBlock renders a code block.
179	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderCodeBlock(node gast.Node, source []byte) {
180		if fenced, ok := node.(*gast.FencedCodeBlock); ok {
181			// Fenced code block with language
182			r.buf.WriteString("```")
183			if lang := fenced.Language(source); len(lang) > 0 {
184				r.buf.Write(lang)
185			}
186			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
187	
188			// Write all lines
189			lines := fenced.Lines()
190			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
191				line := lines.At(i)
192				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
193			}
194	
195			r.buf.WriteString("```")
196			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
197				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
198			}
199		} else if codeBlock, ok := node.(*gast.CodeBlock); ok {
200			// Indented code block
201			lines := codeBlock.Lines()
202			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
203				line := lines.At(i)
204				r.buf.WriteString("    ")
205				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
206			}
207			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
208				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
209			}
210		}
211	}
212	
213	// renderBlockquote renders a blockquote with "> " prefix.
214	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderBlockquote(node *gast.Blockquote, source []byte, depth int) {
215		// Create a temporary buffer for the blockquote content
216		tempBuf := &bytes.Buffer{}
217		tempRenderer := &MarkdownRenderer{buf: tempBuf}
218		tempRenderer.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
219	
220		// Add "> " prefix to each line
221		content := tempBuf.String()
222		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), "\n")
223		for i, line := range lines {
224			r.buf.WriteString("> ")
225			r.buf.WriteString(line)
226			if i < len(lines)-1 {
227				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
228			}
229		}
230	}
231	
232	// renderListItem renders a list item with proper indentation and markers.
233	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderListItem(node *gast.ListItem, source []byte, depth int) {
234		parent := node.Parent()
235		list, ok := parent.(*gast.List)
236		if !ok {
237			r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
238			return
239		}
240	
241		// Add indentation only for nested lists
242		// Document=0, List=1, ListItem=2 (no indent), nested ListItem=3+ (indent)
243		if depth > 2 {

245			r.buf.WriteString(indent)

248		// Add list marker
249		if list.IsOrdered() {
250			fmt.Fprintf(r.buf, "%d. ", list.Start)
251			list.Start++ // Increment for next item
252		} else {
253			r.buf.WriteString("- ")
254		}
255	
256		// Render content
257		r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
258	
259		// Add newline if there's a next sibling
260		if node.NextSibling() != nil {
261			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
262		}
263	}

## Markdown Processing Interface -- Full Analysis

### 1. The Interface

The core markdown processing abstraction is a Go **interface** named `Service`, defined at:

**`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** (lines 31-55)

```go
type Service interface {
    ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)
    ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)
    ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)
    RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)
    RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)
    GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)
    ValidateContent(content []byte) error
    RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)
}
```

It provides tag/mention extraction, property computation, markdown-to-markdown rendering, HTML rendering, snippet generation, content validation, and tag renaming.

### 2. Concrete Implementation

There is exactly **one concrete implementation**: the unexported struct `service` in the same file:

**`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** (lines 57-60)

```go
type service struct {
    md goldmark.Markdown
}
```

It is constructed via the factory function `NewService` (line 85), which accepts functional options (`WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()`) to configure custom goldmark extensions. The `RenderMarkdown` method internally delegates to a helper struct `MarkdownRenderer` at `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go`, but that is not itself an implementation of the `Service` interface -- it is a utility used by the implementation.

There are no other implementations of `markdown.Service` anywhere in the repository (no mocks, no test doubles, no alternative backends).

### 3. Who Constructs/Instantiates the Implementation

`markdown.NewService(...)` is called in **three places** (two production, one test):

| Location | File | Line | Options Used |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Production (primary)** | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` | 48 | `WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()` |
| **Test helper** | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go` | 44 | `WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()` |
| **Test (RSS)** | `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss_test.go` | 54 | No options (bare `NewService()`) |
| **Test (fileserver)** | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` | 427 | `WithTagExtension()` |

The **primary construction point** is in `NewAPIV1Service` at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` line 48. This is called from the main server setup at `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` line 76.

### 4. Which Components Hold References to the Interface

Three structs store a `markdown.Service` field, and one standalone function accepts it as a parameter:

**A. `APIV1Service`** -- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` line 35
```go
type APIV1Service struct {
    ...
    MarkdownService  markdown.Service
    ...
}
```
This is the central API service. It uses the markdown service in:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` lines 108 and 447 -- calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(..., s.MarkdownService)` during memo creation and update
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` line 32 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll(...)` to resolve @mentions
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` line 85 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(...)` for webhook payloads

**B. `RSSService`** -- `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go` line 45
```go
type RSSService struct {
    ...
    MarkdownService markdown.Service
    ...
}
```
Constructed at `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` line 85, receiving `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` (same instance as APIV1Service). Uses `s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML(...)` at line 339 to render memo content into HTML for RSS feed items.

**C. `memopayload.Runner`** -- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` line 16
```go
type Runner struct {
    Store           *store.Store
    MarkdownService markdown.Service
}
```
A batch runner that rebuilds memo payloads. Its `NewRunner` constructor exists (line 19) but is **not called in production code** -- only the standalone function `RebuildMemoPayload` is used directly by `APIV1Service`.

**D. Standalone function `RebuildMemoPayload`** -- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` line 74
```go
func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error
```
Accepts the interface as a parameter (not stored). Called from `APIV1Service` during memo create/update.

### Wiring Summary (Dependency Flow)

```
server.NewServer()
  --> apiv1.NewAPIV1Service()
        --> markdown.NewService(WithTagExtension(), WithMentionExtension())
        --> stores result in APIV1Service.MarkdownService
  --> rss.NewRSSService(..., apiV1Service.MarkdownService)
        --> stores same instance in RSSService.MarkdownService
```

There is a single shared `markdown.Service` instance created at server startup. `APIV1Service` owns it, and the `RSSService` receives a reference to the same instance. There are no alternative implementations, no mocks, and no test doubles -- tests construct real `service` instances via `markdown.NewService(...)`.

### Frontend Note

The frontend (TypeScript/React) has its own completely separate markdown rendering approach using `react-markdown` with remark/rehype plugins. The component `MemoMarkdownRenderer` at `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/MemoMarkdownRenderer.tsx` and its context `MarkdownRenderContext` at `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/MarkdownRenderContext.tsx` do not implement or relate to the Go `markdown.Service` interface. The frontend has no abstraction layer equivalent to the backend interface -- it directly uses the `react-markdown` library with configured plugins inline.
